text: The heath hangs heavy with bilberries now, dark and ready under your hand, more than one picker could ever gather in a day. Fehu is this fullness — not the wealth kept back, but the kind that ripens and asks to be taken while it lasts. What are you leaving on the branch, Anna, waiting for a better morning that the season will not give you?

The phone rings and the voice you have been waiting for says the words at last, and for a moment the room goes still around them. Ansuz is that voice carried on air, the message that finally reaches you across the distance. You have been listening a long while, Anna, turning every silence over in your hands. Now the sound arrives, plain and clear as it always was going to be. What settles in you when you finally hear it?

The door stands open and two cups of coffee sit steaming on the table, one poured before the guest arrived. Gebo is the giving that only works both ways, the seat pulled out and the hand that fills it. Something waits for you here, and it is already warm. What are you leaving on the table, and who is it set for?

The root does not choose the easy way down, Anna, it presses between the stones because the water is below and nowhere else. Every stone it meets forces it to grow thicker, to hold harder, to reach further than it would in soft ground. This is Nauthiz — the need that shapes you by refusing to move aside. What you are pushing against now is not blocking you, it is teaching your roots where the water lies.

The scree slope wants to slide, loose stone over loose stone, all of it moving toward the bottom. One thing holds it — the yew root, threaded deep through the shifting ground, gripping what will not grip itself. This is Eihwaz. You are the root, Anna, not the stone that slides. What in you stays put while the rest gives way?

Around Midsummer the sun rolls low across the sky but never goes under, so the light holds through the night and the shadows only lean without falling. This is Sowilo, the hour when your own strength does not dim when it should. You have been waiting for the dark to give you rest, Anna, and it has not come. What is it in you that keeps burning past the hour you meant to stop?

Two horses climb the mountain together, matching stride for stride, neither pulling ahead nor falling behind. Ehwaz is that steady keeping of pace, the trust that lets one follow the other over loose ground without looking back. Where in your life are two moving as one right now, and does the rhythm still hold?

The egg lies whole in the nest, warm under the feathers, and nothing of what it holds shows yet. Ingwaz is the seed kept in the dark, the growing that happens before there is anything to see. You may wonder if the waiting is empty, but the shell is not idle. What is forming in you now asks only to be left warm a while longer.

The sheep drift into the fold toward evening, slow and without effort, each one finding its own way home. This is Fehu, the wealth that comes when you stop driving it. What in your life is already moving toward you, if you would only let it arrive?

The raven settles on the fencepost and turns its head toward you, in no hurry to leave. It has come with something, and Ansuz is the breath carried in on those black wings. You have been talking over it, filling the quiet before the words could land. What is the raven waiting for you to hear?

The tide draws back over the black sand, taking driftwood out and laying a smooth stone at your feet. This is Gebo, the shore that returns one thing and keeps another with every wave. You cannot hold the water and gather the gift both at once. What are your hands open to now?

The root does not choose the easy way, because there is no easy way down to the water. It presses into the gap between two stones and holds there, growing thin where the ground is hard. This is Nauthiz, the need that shapes you by what it will not let you pass. What in you is pushing toward water it cannot yet see?

The rowan stands alone by the farmhouse, roots holding fast in the dark earth while its crown leans hard in the wind. It never bends all the way, and it never breaks. This is Eihwaz, the part of you that holds through what wants to snap it. What in you is bending now, Anna, and still holding at the root?

The clouds pull back and the sun catches the wet stones, and each one holds a small bright point of light. This is Sowilo, the seeing that comes when the grey finally lifts. What was blurred an hour ago now has an edge you can trace. You know now which way the light falls, Anna.

The one who walks beside you keeps your pace without asking, matching each step over uneven ground. Ehwaz is that quiet agreement, the road shared and lighter for it. Neither of you has to say where you are going.

The egg lies whole in the nest, warm under the down, and nothing of what waits inside shows yet. Ingwaz is this quiet fullness, the shape held before it opens. You cannot hurry the warmth that gathers there. What is forming in you keeps its own hour, and asks only that you stay near.

Fehu is wealth that only counts when it moves, the kind that grows by being shared rather than held. The bread comes hot from the oven, enough for everyone at the table, and no one leaves hungry. What is warm in your hands now is meant to be passed, not stored.

Ansuz is the rune of the message that finds you, the word or the knowing that arrives from somewhere wider than yourself. The raven settles on the fencepost and does not fly, it turns its head and waits for you to grow still. What has been trying to reach you speaks quietest of all.

Gebo is the rune of exchange, of what passes between you and another and holds you both in balance. Watch the shore, how each wave carries one shell up the sand and draws another back into the grey water. Nothing is only kept, nothing is only given. You are standing at that line where the water meets the land.

Nauthiz is the rune of need, of working within what little is left. You keep knitting though the ball of yarn has thinned to a few last turns around your fingers. The needles do not stop, and the row grows shorter than the one before.

Eihwaz is the yew that dies at its heart and lives on at its edges, the thing in you that endures by giving something up. On the steep slope one root holds the loose scree in place while everything around it slides. What in you is still holding, though the ground keeps moving?

Sowilo is the sun's own force, the light that shows a thing plainly for what it is. Around Midsummer that light never quite leaves the sky, and the low hills stay lit through the whole slow night. Nothing is hidden in this hour, not even the small things you had set aside.

Ehwaz is the rune of two moving as one, of trust that holds a shared pace over hard ground. Two horses climb the mountain track together, neither pulling ahead, neither falling back. When one slows on the steep pitch, the other slows with it. This is what it looks like when neither is carrying the other alone.

Ingwaz is the rune of what grows unseen, the new life gathering before it shows. The egg lies whole in the nest, warm under the bird, and nothing of it breaks the surface yet. What is forming in you keeps its own quiet hour.

A little flour still dusts the edge of the board, the part no one thinks to wipe. Fehu is wealth that keeps moving, the warm loaf broken and passed rather than the coin shut in a drawer. The bread comes from the oven with enough for every hand at the table. What in your life is worth more the moment it is shared?

The words hold steady while everything around them blurs, Anna. Ansuz is the rune of the voice that carries meaning across distance, of what one clear message can settle in you. A voice on the phone says the thing you have been waiting to hear, and the room goes quiet around it. What was uncertain has a shape now.

The wave slides up the sand and draws back, giving and taking in one breath, and Gebo is that exchange, a gift held between two hands, kept in balance. Watch it long enough and the giving and the taking blur into one motion. What the water leaves, it also carries off. Nothing here is only kept, and nothing is only lost.

Nauthiz is need, the pressing of what will not be denied. Here the root leaves the soil and works into the gap between stones, finding the one seam that gives. It presses down toward the water, because it must.

The root stays put while the scree slides down around it. Eihwaz is that holding on beneath the surface, the endurance that outlasts the falling away. Loose stone goes where the slope takes it, but the root has gone down into the dark and stayed. What in you keeps its grip while the rest gives way?

Where the cloud thins, Sowilo is the sun coming through at last, clarity after long grey. The light finds the wet stones and turns them from dull to shining, the same stones you walked past all morning. What was dark with rain now holds the whole sky in it. You are seeing what was always there, lit.

Where the trail steepens, one horse steadies and the other keeps its stride to match. Ehwaz is trust that moves, two who carry weight together and neither pulls ahead. The climbing is easier for the pace they hold between them. What in your own step is set by someone walking beside you?

The egg lies whole in the nest, warm under the down, and nothing of what it holds shows on the smooth shell. Ingwaz is the thing gathering unseen, the potential kept close before it takes any form the eye can meet. All the noise of the world falls away, and only the quiet warmth remains. Something in you is being tended in the dark.

You are kneeling on the August heath, fingers stained where the bilberries hang thickest. Fehu is the fruit that came from tending, not wishing — worth that moves between hands. Here, the fullest berries grow low, close to where two people are already standing.

Ansuz is the word carried on air, the sense that reaches past you toward a wider sky, and here it is the plover's call crossing the moor on the breeze. Everything else in the wind falls away, and only that one sound stays clear. You are standing on the open moor, listening for which call is yours.

You stand in the doorway you left open, and coffee waits on the table for two. Gebo is the rune of what passes between hands, the work given and the work received in equal measure. Whatever you are making, it is set out here for someone to meet, not to be carried alone, Anna. Is the second chair filled, or does the work still ask you to make it before it can be shared?

Where the root meets the stone there is a pale scar, worn smooth by the years it took to pass. Nauthiz is the pressure of need, the narrow place a thing must move through to reach what feeds it. The root did not hurry, and still it found the water. What has been pressing on you long enough to leave a mark like that?

The whole slope of loose scree wants to slide, Anna, and it is Eihwaz, the deep root of endurance, that keeps it held. Let the sliding go; watch only the one root threaded through the stone. It holds what no eye above the ground can see.

The sun breaks through at last and glints on the wet stones by the door. Sowilo is that light, Anna, the clearing that shows the house plainly again after grey days. You stand in the yard where the stones are drying, and the way in is lit.

Ehwaz is trust that moves, two keeping one pace along the same track. The one beside you matches your steps without a word, neither pulling ahead nor falling back. Nothing needs saying, because the walking itself is the agreement. You are on the path with a steady companion, and the ground holds you both.

Below the soil the bulb is already dividing, working toward a shape no eye can yet confirm. Ingwaz is that unseen readiness, the seed holding what has not surfaced. Two ways open ahead of you, and only one root is thickening beneath. Which of these, Anna, feels already alive under the ground?
